sources.title: Housing schemes
sources.verified_claim: Enfield states its February 2026 Housing Delivery and Placemaking Plan is a 10-year programme intended to accelerate delivery of thousands of affordable homes and includes a 10-year list of development sites.

sources.title: Current schemes
sources.verified_claim: The live current-schemes page continues to show active 2026 construction and consent milestones, including schemes with construction starts in 2026 and later phase delivery timetables.

sources.title: Planning applications received
sources.verified_claim: Havering publishes weekly lists of newly received planning applications; the official page includes the 14 to 20 July 2026 list, providing a current borough planning-pipeline freshness signal.

sources.title: Jewson Romford expansion approved as Havering moves to unlock local planning
sources.verified_claim: Havering approved a major Romford commercial expansion on 9 July 2026, more than doubling the building footprint on an under-developed site within the Lyon Road Locally Significant Industrial Site and Romford Strategic Development Area.

sources.title: TfL issues Council with Gallows Corner works update
sources.verified_claim: Havering published a TfL works update showing Gallows Corner repairs remain active, with the Council still seeking a firm end-date; this is a current transport-network delivery constraint, not parcel evidence.

sources.title: Housing delivery
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's live Housing Delivery page confirms delivery is being pursued through its Estate Renewal Programme and New Homes Programme, with affordable and sustainable housing as the stated objective.

sources.title: Clapham and Streatham
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's regeneration page records completed and ongoing public-facility investment across Clapham and Streatham; this is area-level context and is not generalized to the sample parcel.

sources.title: West Norwood and Tulse Hill town centres
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth states West Norwood and Tulse Hill are undergoing change supported by around £30 million of capital investment across recent and coming years, including streets, parks and business/industrial-area work.
